content: ITANAGAR: The Governor of Arunachal Pradesh, Lt Gen KT Parnaik, PVSM, UYSM, YSM (Retd.), handed over a cheque of Rs. 2 lakh to Abotani Vidya Niketan, Pachin Colony, Naharlagun, at Lok Bhavan, Itanagar on 23 rd July 2026 to support the strengthening and expansion of the school library. Miss Yanya Karlo,Vice Principal Abotani Vidya Niketan and Shri Sukumaran K, State Coordinator ASVS received the financial assistance. During his visit to the School on 28 th June 2026, the Governor had announced the financial aid for provision of books to enrich the school library and promote learning. A passionate reader himself, the Governor highlighted the transformative power of books in shaping young minds
title: Governor hands over cheque to Abotani Vidya Niketan for strengthening school library

content: . A passionate reader himself, the Governor highlighted the transformative power of books in shaping young minds. He emphasized that reading is one of the most effective ways to nurture curiosity, critical thinking, creativity and lifelong learning among children. He said that a well-equipped library serves as a gateway to knowledge, broadens horizons and inspires students to dream big and achieve their aspirations. The Governor noted that in an age dominated by digital distractions, cultivating a culture of reading among young learners has become more important than ever. He encouraged students to develop the habit of regular reading, describing books as trusted companions that enrich character, strengthen values and open doors to new ideas and opportunities
title: Governor hands over cheque to Abotani Vidya Niketan for strengthening school library

content: . Commending the Arunachal Shiksha Vikas Samiti (ASVS) for its dedicated efforts in promoting quality education through Abotani Vidya Niketan, the Governor appreciated the institution s commitment to academic excellence and character building. He also lauded the students for their discipline, enthusiasm and impressive turnout, expressing confidence that they would grow into responsible citizens and contribute meaningfully to the progress and development of the State and the nation. (PRO to Governor) the News
title: Governor hands over cheque to Abotani Vidya Niketan for strengthening school library

content: PASIGHAT : A District Monitoring Committee, headed by SDO(J) Shri Makbul Siram, on Monday conducted inspections of seven rehabilitation centres across East Siang district, including the Government De-Addiction and Rehabilitation Centre at Jarkong, to review their functioning and ensure compliance with the prescribed guidelines. The inspection team comprised DMO, Dr. Yagling Perme, DDAC Dr. O. Borang, DSP Toni Tatak, DDSE, Adhuk Tabing, DD(ICDS), Mailong Taku, and DIPRO (In-charge), Miding Modi. During the inspection, the committee interacted with the inmates and staff members to assess the availability of basic facilities and services being provided at the rehabilitation centres
title: District Monitoring Committee Inspects Rehabilitation Centres in East Siang

content: . The team also reviewed the overall functioning of the institutions, including healthcare facilities, counseling services, staffing patterns, and the availability of qualified medical professionals to ensure the effective rehabilitation and well-being of the inmates. Speaking during the visit, DDSE Adhuk Tabing highlighted the importance of vocational and skill development activities being facilitated by the District Administration from time to time. He stated that such initiatives help inmates acquire productive skills, promote self-reliance, and support their successful reintegration into society. DD (ICDS) Mailong Taku briefed the managements of the rehabilitation centres on the provisions of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act
title: District Monitoring Committee Inspects Rehabilitation Centres in East Siang

content: . She emphasised that any case involving a juvenile must be reported without delay to the Juvenile Justice authorities or the Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) for necessary legal intervention and protection. The committee also reviewed the maintenance of records, safety measures, hygiene, and the overall living conditions of the inmates. The members advised the managements of all rehabilitation centres to strictly adhere to the prescribed norms, standard operating procedures, and guidelines issued by the competent authorities while ensuring quality care, discipline, and a conducive environment for rehabilitation
title: District Monitoring Committee Inspects Rehabilitation Centres in East Siang

content: . The committee reiterated that regular monitoring and coordinated efforts among the concerned departments are essential to strengthen rehabilitation services and ensure that the centres function in accordance with the objectives of de-addiction, care, and social reintegration. (DIPRO) the News
title: District Monitoring Committee Inspects Rehabilitation Centres in East Siang

content: Seppa: A one-day training programme on Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) for Panchayati Raj Institution (PRI) leaders was held at the District Secretariat here on Wednesday to strengthen grassroots implementation of the flagship rural development mission. The programme was chaired by East Kameng Zilla Parishad Chairperson Pai Pizi Yangfo and coordinated by Deputy Director (Rural Development) Laxmi Dodum. Welcoming the participants, Dodum outlined the objectives of the training and stressed the need to build the capacity of PRI representatives for effective implementation of VB-G RAM G, particularly in the challenging geographical conditions of East Kameng
title: PRI leaders trained on VB-G RAM G implementation in East Kameng

content: . She encouraged participants to actively engage in the sessions and seek clarifications to ensure better execution of the scheme at the grassroots level. The technical sessions were conducted by Rakham Langdo, BDO, Bana-cum-Nodal Officer, VB-G RAM G, East Kameng, who explained the mission s institutional framework, financial management, planning process, transparency and accountability mechanisms, implementation guidelines, and the roles and responsibilities of PRIs under VB-G RAM G and Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G). The training was attended by all Zilla Parishad Members of East Kameng, Block Development Officers, Gram Panchayat Chairpersons, Gram Panchayat Members, Executive Officers (RE), and officials of the RD Department
title: PRI leaders trained on VB-G RAM G implementation in East Kameng

content: . In her concluding remarks, ZPC Pai Pizi Yangfo urged PRI leaders to effectively utilise the knowledge gained during the training and work in close coordination with the Dept of Rural Development to ensure transparent, efficient and successful implementation of VB-G RAM G across the district. (DIPRO) the News
title: PRI leaders trained on VB-G RAM G implementation in East Kameng

content: Daporijo: The District Administration, Upper Subansiri, has successfully initiated the airlifting of essential food commodities to the remote and flood-affected administrative circles of Nilling, Lingdam and Upper Giba, ensuring uninterrupted supply to communities that remain cut off due to extensive road and bridge damage caused by recent monsoon rains. Following heavy rainfall, roads connecting Nilling Circle and Upper Giba Circle were severely damaged due to breaches along the Nyo River and Jao River, while the bridge over the Jao River was washed away, leaving 22 villages of Upper Giba completely disconnected from the district headquarters. In addition, 20 villages under Nilling Circle remain cut off due to the disruption of road connectivity
title: District Administration Airlifts Essential Commodities to Flood-Affected Nilling, Lingdam and Upper Giba

content: . In addition, 20 villages under Nilling Circle remain cut off due to the disruption of road connectivity. The road connectivity to Lingdam and Nilling was also disrupted, making transportation of essential commodities by road impossible. Considering the hardship faced by the affected population, the District Administration, led by the Deputy Commissioner, Upper Subansiri, immediately initiated the process for requisitioning helicopter services. The proposal received the support of local MLA Shri Taniya Soki, and requisitions were submitted to the Directorate of Civil Aviation, Government of Arunachal Pradesh, for airlifting food grains, medicines and other essential supplies
title: District Administration Airlifts Essential Commodities to Flood-Affected Nilling, Lingdam and Upper Giba

content: . The Directorate of Civil Aviation subsequently approved the requisition and issued a revised helicopter sortie schedule for 22 and 23 July 2026. The sorties are transporting rice and other essential commodities from Daporijo to Lingdam and Nilling, ensuring that relief reaches the affected population without delay. The District Administration, in close coordination with the Department of Civil Aviation, District Food Civil Supplies Office, Circle Administrations, Police and other line departments, has made all necessary arrangements at the helipads, including security, crowd management, fire and emergency services, cleanliness, obstacle clearance and other safety measures in accordance with DGCA guidelines
title: District Administration Airlifts Essential Commodities to Flood-Affected Nilling, Lingdam and Upper Giba

content: . The District Administration expresses its sincere gratitude to the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, the Directorate of Civil Aviation, the helicopter crew, all line departments, and local representatives for their timely support and coordinated efforts in ensuring that essential supplies reach some of the most remote and inaccessible areas of Upper Subansiri District. The Administration remains committed to safeguarding the welfare of all residents and will continue to monitor the situation while extending every possible assistance until normal road connectivity is restored. (DIPRO) the News
title: District Administration Airlifts Essential Commodities to Flood-Affected Nilling, Lingdam and Upper Giba

content: Tawang: In a bid to promote sustainable livelihoods and enhance farmers income, the Department of Horticulture, Tawang, organised a one-day mushroom cultivation training programme at the conference hall of the Assistant Commissioner, Kyidphel, on Tuesday under the State Government s Mushroom Mission Initiative. A total of 59 farmers from Kyidphel Block participated in the training programme aimed at encouraging scientific mushroom cultivation as a viable source of income. District Horticulture Officer Koncho Gyatso highlighted the objectives of the Mushroom Mission and urged farmers to adopt scientific cultivation practices. He described mushroom farming as a low-investment, high-return enterprise with significant potential to generate sustainable income and improve rural livelihoods
title: Mushroom cultivation training held in Kyidphel to promote sustainable livelihoods

content: . Assistant Commissioner of Kyidphel, Sange Norbu, encouraged farmers to embrace modern farming techniques to increase productivity and income. He proposed developing a pilot village for mushroom cultivation, expressing confidence that its success would inspire other villages in the block to adopt the initiative. ZPM Kyidphel, Tenzin Monpa, stressed that government welfare schemes can achieve their intended objectives only through active public participation. He urged farmers to make the best use of the training and government support to transform agriculture into a sustainable and profitable livelihood. The programme featured practical demonstrations on Oyster Mushroom cultivation by DHO Koncho Gyatso, who explained substrate preparation, spawning, cultivation techniques and harvesting
title: Mushroom cultivation training held in Kyidphel to promote sustainable livelihoods

content: . Tenzin Yangzom, Block Coordinator of BMMU Lumla, conducted a technical session on Shiitake Mushroom cultivation, highlighting scientific production methods and the commercial potential of the high-value crop. To encourage immediate adoption of the technology, mushroom spawn was distributed to all participating farmers, enabling them to begin cultivation in their respective villages. The training concluded with enthusiastic participation from the farmers, reflecting their growing interest in diversifying agricultural activities and exploring new livelihood opportunities. Officials expressed confidence that the initiative would strengthen rural livelihoods, promote self-employment and contribute to building a resilient farming community in Kyidphel Block through sustainable agriculture
title: Mushroom cultivation training held in Kyidphel to promote sustainable livelihoods

content: History Last Updated on: December 05, 2024 The Agriculture Department , Assam was created in April, 1882 . The Department was then engaged in conducting crop cutting experiments on winter rice, mustard and sugarcane. The crop cutting experiments were then called agricultural experiments. The reason of conducting crop cutting experiments was to assess productiveness of land to prepare assessment proposals during settlement. There was no agricultural expert in the Department till 1897. In 1893 , an Agricultural Conference was held in Simla. In accordance with the recommendations of this conference, Government of India deputed Sir E. Buck to Assam in 1895 to discuss with Assam Government about the recommendations. Sir E
title: History | Agriculture & Horticulture | Government of Assam, India

content: . Buck to Assam in 1895 to discuss with Assam Government about the recommendations. Sir E. Buck advocated appointment of an Agricultural Expert to (1) ascertain agricultural defects and (2) introduce agricultural improvements. In the year 1897, Mr. B. C. Basu a Deputy Collector of Bengal and a graduate of an Agricultural College in England was appointed as Assistant Director. Although Assam was a separate province it was amalgamated with Eastern Bengal in 1905. In the new province of Eastern Bengal and Assam the Agriculture Department was separated in 1907 form the combined Department of Land Records and Agriculture. After the creation of a separate Department, expansion of the Department took place quickly
title: History | Agriculture & Horticulture | Government of Assam, India

content: . After the creation of a separate Department, expansion of the Department took place quickly. Assam became a separate province again in 1912 when the Agriculture Department was again combined with that of Land Records and continued up to 1922. In 1923 three allied Department of Agriculture, Cooperation and Industries were combined.

content: RTPS Services Last Updated on: December 05, 2024 The Assam Right to Public Service Act in 2012, enacted by the Government of Assam, is an act to provide for the delivery of notified public services to the people of the state of Assam within the stipulated time limit and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto. This Act came into force across all districts of the state, except for the Sixth Schedule areas. However, the Act has now been extended and adopted in the Sixth Schedule Districts which includes Bodoland Territorial Council (BTC), Dima Hasao Autonomous Territorial Council (DHATC) and Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council (KAAC). This should be done before seeds are kept in storage. There are various steps to be followed viz. cleaning (wet and dry), winnowing, sieving, drying, tests to ascertain the dryness of seeds. This involves taking the cleaned seed and coating them with a chemical, usually antimicrobial or fungicidal, to make them more robust for the field. content: History Last Updated on: December 05, 2024 The Agriculture Department , Assam was created in April, 1882 . The Department was then engaged in conducting crop cutting experiments on winter rice, mustard and sugarcane. The crop cutting experiments were then called agricultural experiments. The reason of conducting crop cutting experiments was to assess productiveness of land to prepare assessment proposals during settlement. There was no agricultural expert in the Department till 1897. In 1893 , an Agricultural Conference was held in Simla. In accordance with the recommendations of this conference, Government of India deputed Sir E. Buck to Assam in 1895 to discuss with Assam Government about the recommendations. Sir E
title: History | Agriculture & Horticulture | Government of Assam, India

content: . Buck to Assam in 1895 to discuss with Assam Government about the recommendations. Sir E. Buck advocated appointment of an Agricultural Expert to (1) ascertain agricultural defects and (2) introduce agricultural improvements. In the year 1897, Mr. B. C. Basu a Deputy Collector of Bengal and a graduate of an Agricultural College in England was appointed as Assistant Director. Although Assam was a separate province it was amalgamated with Eastern Bengal in 1905. In the new province of Eastern Bengal and Assam the Agriculture Department was separated in 1907 form the combined Department of Land Records and Agriculture. content: . It was a part of Union Territory of Goa, Daman Diu till 30th May 1987 when it was carved out of form a separate state. Goa covers an area of 3702 square kilometers and comprises two Revenue district viz North Goa and South Goa. content: . Preamble India has achieved significant economic growth over the past decades, but the progress in health has not been commensurate. Despite notable gains in improving life expectancy, reducing fertility, maternal and child mortality, reducing morbidity and mortality due to major communicable diseases and addressing other health priorities, the rates of improvement have been insufficient, falling short on several national and global targets. Indian healthcare delivery system has come a long way in providing primary, preventive and curative health care with its three tier system- primary health centre catering a group of villages, secondary level health centre located at district level, and medical college hospitals constituting the tertiary level located in the relatively big cities
title: NCDC_e-Sanjeevani-guidelines_29.06.20-1.pdf

content: . Besides, there are few advanced medical institutes of national importance having clinical, teaching and research facilities in many super-specialties. In spite of nationally driven health programs under National Health Mission (NHM), access and fulfilment of healthcare needs for bulk of the population in rural areas is still inadequate. The biggest challenge is posed by the lack of medical human resource- doctors and specialists in rural areas, inadequate capacities of the doctors/ mid-level providers in the PHCs/HWCs and lack of organised continuum of care. There is also the problem of prescription and dispensing of drugs in rural areas close to the community. These challenges can be reasonably effectively addressed utilising information technology in delivering healthcare services
title: NCDC_e-Sanjeevani-guidelines_29.06.20-1.pdf

Government Central Workshop :- It undertakes the repair and maintenance of light vehicles of Raj Bhawan, Chief Minister/ VIPs, State Civil Secretariat and other Government departments on payment basis. Transport department is nodal department to decide the purchase policy of light vehicles, accordingly Government Central Workshop renders its technical advice to State Government for framing the policies of purchase of light vehicles and undertakes the inspection of light vehicles which are purchased by Government departments/ Boards/ Corporations Authorities through Director, Supplies Disposal, Haryana

content: Introduction Publish Date : July 2, 2018 Office of the Director General State Transport is responsible for providing well-coordinated, economical, safe and efficient transport action services to the public of the State. Haryana Roadways, a State Government Undertaking, is the principal service provider for passenger transport in the State. It has bus fleet being operated by 24 depots, each headed by a General Manager, and 13 sub-depots functioning under the depot concerned. These services are being provided to every part of the State as well as to important destinations in the neighbouring States.Haryana Roadways plies on an average 13.00 Lac Km every day. Over the years Haryana Roadways has earned a name for itself for the range and quality of services provided by it
title: Introduction

content: . Over the years Haryana Roadways has earned a name for itself for the range and quality of services provided by it. In tune with the emerging requirements of the traveling public, Haryana Roadways has undertaken a series of new initiatives to provide better services to its clients. New Volvo AC bus services Saarthi have been introduced on certain routes. Some of the trips are also touching the Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport and the domestic Airport Delhi. Haryana Standard Ordinary Buses popularly known as Haryana Shakti now embedded with BS VI norms- For the first time in Haryana, buses with BS VI norms have been introduced in Haryana Roadways. This is a 59 seater bus having a luggage storage box for the passengers alongwith various other facilities
title: Introduction

content: . This is a 59 seater bus having a luggage storage box for the passengers alongwith various other facilities. BS VI buses are Anti Pollutant Buses which is a justified step by the Government to control environmental pollution. Haryana Roadways Mini Buses are the pink colored buses which is the symbol of Beti Padhao Beti Bacho slogan given by Hon ble Prime Minister. These buses are introduced in Haryana Roadways for the safety and security of female candidates going for School Colleges from and to various Villages Cities of Haryana. These buses are fully furnished with their surveillance cameras for the security of girls student. The passenger amenities at the Bus Stands have been significantly upgraded to make travel a pleasant experience
title: Introduction

content: . The passenger amenities at the Bus Stands have been significantly upgraded to make travel a pleasant experience. New Bus Stands are proposed to be constructed with a futuristic vision and will be comparable with similar facilities available anywhere in the world. All efforts are being made to ensure that the passengers get hygienic food/eatables at fixed rates at the bus stands. Water cooler with filters are being provided at important bus stands. Haryana Roadways is providing free travelling facility and concessional travel facility to a large number of categories. The Department plans to install GPS in its buses and CCTV Cameras on all major Bus Stands.
title: Introduction

title: Child Help Line (CHL)

Calls have been regularly received, 49675 calls have been answered from 01.09.2023 to 11.11.2024.
title: Child Help Line (CHL)

content: Our Services The scheme provides financial support for service delivery and required manpower to ensure immediate and long-term care for targeted women. The components under Mission Shakti have the broad objectives of either protecting or assisting women who are victims of violence or in difficult circumstances or for empowering women. The objectives of the Mission are as under: Emergency/ Immediate services short-term care Putting in place mechanisms for providing a continuum of support and care for women affected by violenceand women in distress through dedicated 24 hours helpline by a national toll-free number and integrated services such as temporary shelter, legal aid, psycho-social counselling

content: . 01 Institutional Care for long term support The long-term institutional care component, inter alia, includes taking care of the needs of women right from the conception stage till the time they need such care and support because of their physical, financial and sociological status due to various factors. 02 Behaviour Change Communication for dignity and prevention of crime and violence against women This would include large scale awareness programs and community engagement for gender sensitisation, advocacy, training and capacity building of all duty bearers, service providers and stakeholders through inter-ministerial convergence. 03
